evals.prompt: I'm board chair of Valley Literacy Council in Yakima, WA ($1.8M, 22 staff). Our founder and ED, Margaret, started the org 27 years ago and told us she'll retire in June 2028. She holds nearly all the major donor relationships. We have a program director who might be a candidate. We've never done succession planning. What should the board do?
evals.expected_output: Separates an immediate emergency plan from a long-range plan, forms a transition committee, runs a readiness assessment naming founder's-syndrome and donor-concentration risk, assesses the internal candidate against a competency framework, decides the path, sets a realistic timeline and bounded handoff with donor re-introduction, routing search mechanics elsewhere.
assertions: Distinguishes an emergency succession plan from a long-range succession plan and recommends ratifying an emergency plan now regardless of the known retirement
Recommends a separate transition committee of a few board members distinct from the standing governance committee
Explicitly names founder's-syndrome and donor-concentration risk and recommends a structured donor/funder relationship transfer plan
Recommends assessing the program director against a written leadership competency framework with a development plan, not tenure alone
Calls for a documented decision among internal promotion, open search, or interim-then-search, with a realistic search timeline and extra runway for a founder transition
Recommends defining Margaret's post-departure role with bounded authority and a capped handoff period to avoid shadow leadership, and hands search mechanics to the executive search skill

evals.prompt: we don't have an emergency succession plan for our ED. can you give me one to fill in? small org, 6 staff, deputy director is Luis Ortega
evals.expected_output: A fill-in emergency succession plan naming the acting authority and backup, authority limits, board contact, signatory changes, document locations without passwords, communication order and the path to a longer-term decision, ratified by board vote with an annual review.
assertions: Provides a template naming Luis Ortega as acting authority with a backup
Spells out what the acting leader may and may not do without board approval, including signing thresholds
Lists signatory changes (bank, payroll, grants portals) and where key accounts/documents are stored, explicitly without writing passwords into the plan
Requires ratification by board vote recorded in minutes with an annual review date and confirming named people have agreed
Includes notification order and a deadline for the board to meet to decide interim vs. search

evals.prompt: Our ED had a stroke last night and won't be back for at least 3 months, maybe ever. We have no plan. The board is freaking out — some want to post the ED job tomorrow. What do we do this week?
evals.expected_output: Stands up emergency acting authority with defined limits immediately, warns against rushing an open search, and points to the interim workplan, communications and search skills for their parts.
assertions: Recommends immediately naming an acting leader by board vote with written scope, authority limits and signing thresholds, plus a board point of contact
Advises against posting the ED job immediately, noting rushed searches are a common cause of failed placements and the board should first decide interim vs. search
Covers urgent signatory/account access steps (bank, payroll) owned by a named board officer
Defines an interim arrangement with a scope and end/review date rather than open-ended, routing the detailed interim workplan to the executive transitions skill
Routes staff/funder announcement drafting to the executive communications or change management skill

should_not_trigger.query: Our ED is leaving in March — help us write the position profile and set the salary range for the search.
I'm the interim ED starting Monday — help me draft my 90-day workplan and mandate.
